title: Show the build commit in athena --version
summary: Make `athena --version` print the package version plus the short git commit hash the binary was built from, with a dirty marker, and `unknown` when git is unavailable. Do it with a build script in the athena-cli crate and add a test.

defaults_applied.how: The build script is Rust (build.rs); no shell or other non-Rust files.
Weigh vergen/shadow-rs against a ~30-line build.rs and record the choice.
Add a --version test in the athena-cli tests; clippy and tests stay clean.
Verifier runs the built binary's --version and compares it with git HEAD.
Read 'which build setup adopted' as: identify the exact commit of the running binary.

assumptions: `athena --version` is the clap `version` flag on the `Cli` struct in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, currently printing only the Cargo package version.
The wanted output is the short HEAD hash, with a dirty marker. Nothing else is added, such as build date or target.
A small build.rs that shells out to `git` is enough and avoids a new dependency. A crate like vergen is the alternative under the buy-first default.
Only the athena binary's `--version` changes. `--json` outputs and records are untouched.

acceptance_criteria.text: After `cargo build -p athena-cli`, running `target/debug/athena --version` prints the package version followed by the short git commit hash of HEAD (for example `athena 0.1.0 (abc1234)`), and marks a dirty working tree (for example `-dirty`). Check by running it and comparing with `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
When the build has no git metadata (source copy without .git, or git missing), the build still succeeds and the version shows `unknown` in place of a hash. Check by building from a copy without .git.
The commit is captured at build time and rebuilds when HEAD changes (build.rs emits rerun-if-changed for the git HEAD and ref files). It is not hard-coded.
A test in crates/athena-cli/tests asserts that `--version` output contains the version and a commit hash or `unknown`. `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
The build-script approach (a small build.rs, as opposed to a crate such as vergen) is recorded with a short reason in a code comment or docs. No new non-Rust files are added.

out_of_scope: Build date, target triple or rustc version in the version string
Recording the commit in job records or other command output
Changes to CI workflows, setup.sh or other governance files
departures: Slightly lower cost and tighter time than the reference: the change is small and confined to one crate. The risk is that the build runs from a copy without .git.
